components.description: One-semester paid parental leave for full-time tenure and tenure-track faculty (and eligible NTT faculty and librarians) who become biological or adoptive parents of a child under five; the pay is the member's own accrued sick leave, then the member-funded Sick Leave Bank.
components.mechanism_note: A dedicated parental leave funded from sick leave and a sick bank stays employer-paid leave as a mechanism (V1); its pay is coded own_balance (R1d).
components.faculty_group_note: Art. 27.3.5(b)(1): 'All full-time tenure and tenure-track faculty members'; also (2) NTT faculty not funded by grants, contracts or gifts with three years of full-time service, (3) librarians with at least four months of service.

components.duration_note: One semester for academic-year faculty; 24 weeks for librarians and faculty on calendar-basis appointments. Sick leave or the Sick Leave Bank may not extend it unless medically indicated.
components.pay_fraction: paid leave, drawn from the member's accrued sick leave, then the Sick Leave Bank

components.return_obligation: return for one year of full-time service (one and a half years if adjacent to a sabbatical)

notes: Reference date 2018-03-13. The 2014-2017 agreement expired 2017-06-30 but stays in force until a successor is executed (Art. 37.2); the document's version notes the 2017-2020 successor was ratified 2018-07-19, after the reference date. T93-123 and T76-081 carry their own dates and were captured 2017-03-15.

Calendar: the documents state a semester calendar ('one-semester paid leave', semester-based terms) but no term length for academic-year faculty, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. The 24 weeks stated for calendar-basis appointees is their parental-leave length, not a term length.

Parental leave pay (c1): Art. 27.3.5 calls it a 'one-semester paid leave', but requires the member to use accrued sick leave and, if that is insufficient, the Sick Leave Bank, which members fund with their own sick days; no employer shortfall is stated. Coded payer own_balance under R1d, whose UMass Lowell MSP example (one semester from own sick leave, then the member-funded Sick Leave Bank) is the same structure. Read under R1c instead, the leave would count one semester employer-paid.

Chain, birth parent: parental leave 1 semester (c1; paid from own sick leave, then the Sick Leave Bank) with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) concurrent from its start, and state-law maternity leave (c3, length not in sources) concurrent with FMLA; tenure decision year delayed one year (c11).
Chain, non-birth parent: parental leave 1 semester (c1) with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) concurrent from its start; tenure decision year delayed one year (c11).

Sick leave (c4) and the Sick Leave Bank (c5) are left unlinked: they fund the parental leave (already coded as c1's own_balance pay) and the member's own illness generally; Art. 27.3.5(d) bars using them to extend the parental leave unless medically indicated.

Not components: bereavement leave (27.3.6), domestic violence leave (27.4), witness leave (5.6), union release time (5.5-5.8), sabbatical leave (Appendix C; for scholarship, not usable for a birth), the 43-week librarian workyear (20.10), librarian release time for study (20.11.2), the Dependent Care Assistance Program and Health and Welfare Fund (no leave or pay terms stated), and NTT continuity-of-service rules (21.11; FMLA-qualifying absences do not break service for faculty without benefits).
T93-123 mentions 'life and disability insurance' maintained during FMLA leave; no saved document describes a disability plan, so none is coded.

Cross-references not saved: the Massachusetts statute providing maternity/adoptive leave (T93-123, unnamed; c3); Small Necessities Leave Act (27.3.3(f)); University sabbatical leave policy T66-049 as amended by T73-065 (T76-081 s. 4.13); Policy on Faculty Consulting and Outside Activities T96-047 and the conflict-of-interest policies (27.3.5(e)); Trustee Implementation Guidelines (2.3); Health and Welfare Fund Agreement and Declaration of Trust (27.9); Tuition Remission Policy (27.10); FSU 2017-2020 successor agreement (after the reference date). FMLA itself is saved among the statute texts (29 U.S.C. 2611, 2612).
